analysis.title: 500 Railway Companies, 8,000 Miles Of Track: Goldman's Molavi Explains Why The Builders Rarely Keep A Bubble's Value
key_insights: Molavi (Goldman) separates technology, bubbles and terminal value. A technology can be transformative and still not create immediate value for the capital that financed it. The tulip, railway and internet manias left the underlying thing in place, but early capital was hurt when valuation decoupled from revenue and cash flow.

Molavi's historical parallel is British railway mania in the 1840s: 500 new companies built 8,000 miles of track at a cost above the country's entire national income. The value ended up with the economies that used the infrastructure, not the builders.

Dot-com version: Cisco and Qualcomm 'thrive and then falter', and 360networks, AltaVista and Webvan faded. The fiber was laid and later users of it captured the value. Molavi says the value of innovation is not in question, but the price paid and the timing of the return are.

Molavi argues this cycle is more interdependent than 2000. Every industry is now tech, and AI spending is circular: the Nvidia and OpenAI deal, Nvidia's stake in Intel, Oracle buying Nvidia GPUs, hyperscalers holding stakes in AI startups. He calls much of 2026 a 'mega fomo trade' in which fear of under-investing outweighed the risk of investing too early or too much.

Momentum mechanism: with the S&P driven by 5 to 10 stocks, and over 60% of year-to-date returns six months into the year coming from 6 stocks (35% from one), a growing share of assets sits in index-tracking wrappers that must buy what rises and have no view on fair value. Molavi says a large part of Nvidia's gains was fundamental, but a large part was technical, which works on the way down as well. The momentum factor gave back all of its 2026 gains in a matter of weeks.

Valuation: the S&P forward P/E is about 18x versus 10.4x at the March 2009 trough, 13.3x in March 2020 and 15.7x in October 2022, if last week was the low. Molavi's verdict is 'cheaper rather than cheap'. He concedes the comparison ignores growth, with US earnings still growing 30%-plus, but that growth depends on the AI capex cycle, so 18x on peak-cycle earnings differs from 18x on trough earnings.

Zero Hedge's own commentary (not Molavi's): Nvidia fell as much as 8% after Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a woman US officials suspect is a Chinese spy, and the board opened an independent probe. It frames this as key-man risk for the AI trade. Nvidia is described as back at 18-month lows below $4 trillion after peaking at $5.8 trillion.

Zero Hedge's own commentary: the funding is still expanding despite last week's selloff. OpenAI reportedly closed roughly $11 billion of initial funding at a $1.25 trillion valuation, Anthropic is reportedly targeting an $80-100 billion IPO before Thanksgiving, and hyperscalers exceeded their full-year debt forecast with seven weeks left in 2026.

Zero Hedge's own commentary: the dot-com bust mostly hurt shareholders and the telecom bust also hurt bondholders. This buildout is increasingly financed with debt, SPVs and vendor financing among the same few companies, so if value migrates away from the builders the losses may extend beyond equity prices to balance sheets across the market.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell as much as 8% after the CEO admitted an affair with a woman US officials suspect is a Chinese spy and the board opened an independent probe. This is Zero Hedge's reporting, not a Goldman rating action.

earnings_insights: Molavi cites US earnings growing at a 30%-plus clip, a figure he says is not accounted for in the P/E comparison with past trough multiples. He argues much of that growth would turn if the AI capex cycle turns, which would make the 18x forward multiple a multiple on peak-cycle earnings.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Molavi calls the market 'cheaper rather than cheap' at 18x, if last week was the low. The comparison omits growth rates, and the multiple is on earnings that depend on the AI capex cycle.

risk_factors: Value in an infrastructure bubble tends to accrue to later users rather than the builders, so AI infrastructure spenders may not capture the return on their capex.
AI capex cycle turning would reduce the 30%-plus US earnings growth that supports the 18x forward multiple.

Circular financing and interdependence among Nvidia, OpenAI, Oracle, Intel and the hyperscalers, with debt, SPVs and vendor financing, could spread losses to bondholders and balance sheets (Zero Hedge's view).
Key-man and governance risk at Nvidia following the CEO controversy and the independent board probe.
Momentum unwind: index-tracking and systematic flows that bought winners on the way up can sell on the way down.
vol_and_positioning: The momentum factor gave back all of its 2026 gains in a matter of weeks.
Index concentration: the S&P is driven by 5 to 10 stocks, at times 1 or 2. Over 60% of year-to-date returns six months into the year came from 6 stocks, 35% from one.
Passive, ETF, market-neutral and systematic funds treat price momentum as an input and are never sellers while stocks rise, which Molavi says amplifies the decline once prices fall.
Zero Hedge references Molavi's earlier note on crowded funds playing 'stop bingo', described as a $3 trillion air pocket over two days. That flows-side note is not part of this document.
geopolitical: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a woman US officials suspect is a Chinese spy, and Nvidia's board opened an independent probe.

tension_points.bull_case: The value of AI is not in question and a huge amount of Nvidia's appreciation was fundamental and deserved. US earnings are growing 30%-plus, and the S&P at 18x forward is cheaper than the March 2009, 2020 and 2022 comparison points listed only partly (it was lower at each trough).
tension_points.bear_case: Builders of bubble-era infrastructure rarely keep the value, as in the 1840s railways and the dot-com fiber. An 18x multiple on peak-cycle capex-driven earnings differs from 18x on trough earnings. Financing is increasingly debt, SPVs and vendor financing among the same few companies.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The AI capex cycle turning, which would remove much of the 30%-plus earnings growth supporting the 18x multiple.
